teaching.hint: Which unresolved elements can the current value answer, and how could they be kept so none is overlooked?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Unresolved requests can be kept in nonincreasing value order; a strictly greater arrival resolves a suffix of them. A second virtual lap supplies wrapped successors.
solution_outline.approach: Scan two virtual copies of the array. Keep pending original indices in a stack; at each value resolve and remove every smaller pending top, assigning the current value. Push indices only during the first lap. Leave unresolved answers at the prescribed sentinel.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Pending indices increase from bottom to top and their values are nonincreasing. No pending request has encountered a strictly greater value after its own position; resolved requests have their first such value.
solution_outline.correctness: An arriving value larger than a lower stack entry is also larger than every entry above it, so top removal exposes every request it can answer. A pending index has not previously encountered a greater successor, making the current arrival its first. All other positions in its circular order occur within two laps. A request still pending after its full successor range has no greater value anywhere and remains unresolved even through any repeated prefix; therefore the final unresolved sentinels are correct.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n)` time and `O(n)` auxiliary space: each original index is pushed once and popped at most once across two laps.
solution_outline.pitfall: Equal values must stay pending; using a non-strict greater comparison answers requests incorrectly, especially in an all-equal array.

common_wrong_turns: Equal values must stay pending; using a non-strict greater comparison answers requests incorrectly, especially in an all-equal array.
source_fidelity_notes: Retained strict first-successor order, wrapping, singleton behavior, negative values, and the specified ambiguous sentinel.
Used the canonical strict comparator and tie rule with the correct nonincreasing invariant; omitted its false strict-stack and second-lap re-push amortization claims.
